conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 32 years old and female. I'm here because I've been having numbness and tingling in my right hand, especially when I'm typing on the keyboard. It's been going on for about six months, but it's been more persistent over the last month.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any trauma, repetitive strain, or prior conditions affecting your right hand or arm? Have you undergone any previous treatments or interventions for this issue?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't think I've had any trauma to my hand, and I haven't had any prior treatments for this. It's just been something I've been dealing with while I work at the keyboard all day.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any weakness, pain, or changes in sensation in other parts of your body, such as your arm, neck, or shoulder? Additionally, have you been diagnosed with any systemic conditions like diabetes or thyroid disorders?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any weakness, pain, or changes in sensation in my arm, neck, or shoulder. I also don't have any systemic conditions like diabetes or thyroid disorders.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the specific pattern of numbness and tingling in your right hand, such as whether it affects your fingers, palm, or wrist, and whether it is constant or intermittent?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The numbness and tingling are mostly in my thumb, index finger, and a little in my middle finger. It's been constant now, but it started off and on for about six months. It's worse when I'm typing, and I feel some pain then too.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any previous neurological or musculoskeletal evaluations for this condition? If so, what were the findings?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any previous neurological or musculoskeletal evaluations for this condition. I just started noticing the symptoms a few months ago and haven't seen anyone about it before today.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies, such as an X-ray, MRI, or EMG, to evaluate the cervical spine or upper extremities?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any imaging studies like an X-ray, MRI, or EMG to evaluate my cervical spine or upper extremities. This is the first time I've been seeing a doctor about this issue.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any neck pain, stiffness, or radiating pain from your neck to your arm that could suggest cervical spine involvement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any neck pain or stiffness, and I don't feel any radiating pain from my neck to my arm. I didn't even think about that, but I don't believe that's part of it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any nerve conduction studies or electromyography (EMG) to evaluate for conditions such as carpal tunnel syndrome?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't undergone any nerve conduction studies or EMG to evaluate for carpal tunnel syndrome. The doctor just mentioned ordering one as part of the plan, so that hasn't been done yet.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any changes in grip strength or difficulty performing tasks that require fine motor skills in your right hand?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yes, I have noticed that my grip strength is a little weaker in my right hand, and it's been harder to do things that require fine motor skills, like typing or using the mouse. It feels like my hand just doesn't have the same strength or coordination as before.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any night pain or waking up due to hand discomfort?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any night pain or waking up due to hand discomfort. The numbness and tingling are constant during the day, but they don't bother me enough to wake me up at night.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any physical examination or imaging studies to evaluate the cervical spine or upper extremities?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't undergone any physical examination or imaging studies to evaluate the cervical spine or upper extremities. The doctor did do some physical tests during the visit, like bending my wrist and tapping on my forearm, but no imaging has been done yet.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe any specific physical examination findings from the doctor's tests, such as whether there was any tenderness, weakness, or sensory deficits identified during the examination?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The doctor bent my wrist and that caused pain, and when he tapped on the inside of my wrist or forearm, it caused a shooting pain and I grimaced. He also noticed that I have less grip strength in my right hand and that I have numbness and tingling in my thumb, index finger, and middle finger.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe if you have experienced any pain, numbness, or tingling in your arm, neck, or shoulder, or if you have noticed any changes in your posture or activities that might be contributing to your symptoms?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have pain in my arm, neck, or shoulder, and I haven't noticed any changes in my posture. The main issue is with my right hand, especially when I'm typing or using the mouse. It feels like my hand is getting numb and tingly all the time, and it hurts when I move my wrist.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any recent imaging studies, such as an MRI of the cervical spine or wrist, or nerve conduction studies to evaluate for carpal tunnel syndrome or cervical radiculopathy?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any recent imaging studies like an MRI of the cervical spine or wrist, or nerve conduction studies. The doctor mentioned ordering an EMG and nerve conduction study, but that hasn't been done yet. I'm waiting to hear about the results of that test.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone nerve conduction studies or EMG testing for the right hand, and if so, what were the results?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't undergone nerve conduction studies or EMG testing for the right hand yet. The doctor mentioned ordering that test, but I'm still waiting for the results.
